From your neighbors

Yards that made it through the valley year

"My grandfather planted a Blenheim apricot behind this house in the sixties. When it finally died, Amparo found me the same variety bare-root in January and showed me where the old one stood too close to the fence."

Esteban M., Modesto Sample review

"Our west wall bakes every afternoon. They talked us out of a sycamore, said the roots would find the slab, and sold us a Chinese pistache instead. Third summer now and the living room is noticeably cooler."

"Come for tomato starts every April. They label which ones set fruit in the heat and which quit in July, which no other place bothers to tell you."
